short_answer: Paul Leiner's page is live and selling. On 17 Nov 2026 it offered a college basketball play dated that day, listed eight access packages with prices and showed a long list of record totals. That much is real. What the site does not show is who runs it: there is no company name, no street address and no phone number, only a Gmail address.

Every record on the page is kept by the seller, and much of it is chosen. A long "Top Play Breakdown" lists only winning plays. Several totals do not match each other, such as a college basketball record shown as 154-137 in one place and 178-154-5 in another, and the bio says both "since 2008" and "14 years of winning".

We found no independent post from anyone who bought his picks, good or bad. With no outside evidence either way, the reader has only the seller's own numbers to go on. If you buy, buy a single day, and log every pick yourself.

guarantee: The daily play carries the line "MUST WIN OR NEXT 3 DAYS FREE" (also written "Must Win or Three Free Days"). The rating system says top rated 3000* plays "Will Have Guarantee Attached." A loss earns more picks, not money back.

The PlayersInsider terms say there are no exchanges and no refunds, and that "all sales are final." They add that only individual daily purchases are backed by free service, and that on multi day packages there is no guarantee of extra days if one of those days loses. The site also says it is not liable for any losses. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves.

claims_note: Some totals on the same page disagree. The college basketball record appears as "154-137" and as "178-154-5". The 2025 NFL season appears as "13 winning weeks out of the 18 NFL Regular Season weeks" and as "14 out of 22 Winning NFL Weeks". The overall MLB record appears as 327-280-2 and 328-275-1.
The bio says he started on the site in 2008, which would be 18 years, while the same bio says "I have 14 years of winning on my side."

The page also lists monthly winning days, and these include losing months, such as 13 winning days out of 31 in August 2026 and 13 out of 31 in January 2026. That is more candid than the "Top Play Breakdown" list, which shows only plays that won.

Taken at face value, the seller's own overall run of 5,088 wins and 4,302 losses is about 54% winners, only a little above the roughly 52.4% needed to break even at standard -110 odds, and only if the record is complete.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of his picks kept by a third party, no contest results, and no court or regulator record.

What the seller publishes: totals by sport and star rating, a list of winning top plays going back months, monthly counts of winning days, and the day's free 100* play. The site does not say who grades these or how, and it shows no list of losing plays alongside the winners.
The PlayersInsider homepage lists 13 handicappers, most priced at $29 to $44 a day with "must win" free day offers. All of them are sold by the same unnamed operator.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence about Paul Leiner is nonexistent in what we could find. The only posts under his name are his own promotional threads. Below is what we checked and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no independent post from anyone who bought Paul Leiner picks, on any site or in any year we could search. CapperTek has a page for PlayersInsider.com with no reviews or complaints. The Cappers Forum threads that turn up in search are posted by the seller to promote his plays, and that forum refused to load for us. Our own library of buyer posts had no mention of him or of PlayersInsider. With no posts either way there is no smoke to report; there is simply nothing independent to go on. Our Reddit search was partial. The Reddit archive's full text search timed out on 17 Nov 2026, so we checked our saved copy of ten betting subreddits and one WagerTalk thread instead. None of them mentioned him or PlayersInsider.
CapperTek's PlayersInsider.com page said there were no reviews or complaints for the site. The reviews shown lower on that page are about other services.
Web searches of Covers, Sportsbook Review, TheRX and general search results found no buyer review, complaint or results thread about Paul Leiner or Pleiner.

conflicts: The records, the "#1 rated" claim and the list of winning plays are all published by the site that sells his picks. The site does not name its owner, so we cannot tell how the handicapper and the operator are related.
strengths: Prices for every package are published, and a single day costs $29 to $39.
The page posts a free daily play and dates its top plays, and its monthly winning day counts include losing months.
The terms state plainly that there are no refunds and that only daily purchases carry the free days offer.
concerns: No company name, street address or phone number; the only contact is a Gmail address.
Every record is kept by the seller, the top play list shows only winners, and several totals on the same page disagree.
The guarantee gives free days, not money, and covers daily purchases only. All sales are final.
We found no independent buyer reports, positive or negative.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and free days. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits or more picks.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: His page is live, sells dated daily picks and posts prices. The site that sells them does not name a company or give an address, every record is kept by the seller, and we found no buyer posts about him either way. We also found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Paul Leiner cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 a daily play cost $39 (also shown as $29 in the write up). Access ran $79 for 2 days, $149 for 7 days, $399 for 30 days, $999 for 100 days and $1599 for 180 days.
Does Paul Leiner have a verified record?

No. The page shows totals such as 167-100-2 over 67 days and 5,088-4,302-115 overall, plus a list of winning top plays, all published by the seller. Some totals on the page contradict each other. We found no independent, time stamped log.

For $29 to $39 you get one day of picks with a free days offer if the main play loses. What is unproven is whether the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over time, and even the seller's own overall run is only about 54% winners. Nothing refunds your betting losses.
